summary: IBM's chess machine, the first computer to beat a reigning world champion in a match. After winning the 1997 rematch against Garry Kasparov it was retired, and its two racks went to museums.

image.alt: One of the two Deep Blue cabinets

events.note: Begins at Carnegie Mellon University as ChipTest; the team joins IBM in 1989.
Wins its first game against Kasparov; it loses that match 4 to 2.
Wins the rematch 3½ to 2½ and is retired by IBM.

image.alt: A Deep Blue cabinet at the Computer History Museum
image.caption: Deep Blue at the Computer History Museum.
image.credit: Anton Chiang from Cupertino, CA, USA

events.note: One rack is at the Computer History Museum, the other at the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History.

cause: Retired after winning its rematch against the world chess champion.
